key_themes: Semiconductor selloff accelerates — SOX index drops 6.7% as chip stocks reverse H1 gains
Meta cloud entry crushes AI-infrastructure neoclouds (CoreWeave, Nebius)
Dow hits all-time high (52,900) while Nasdaq falls 1.6% — rare divergence
Weak June jobs report (57K vs 115K est.) lifts Fed rate-cut hopes
Tesla beats delivery estimates but stock tanks on margin concerns

stocks.reason: Shares surged ~9-11% after Bloomberg reported Meta is launching a cloud business to sell excess AI compute capacity, entering competition with AWS/Azure/GCP and threatening neocloud providers.
Shares jumped ~13% after Rivian raised its 2026 delivery guidance to 65K-70K vehicles (up from 62K-67K), following Q2 deliveries of 12,194 units.
Stock fell ~7.5% despite reporting blowout Q2 deliveries of 480,126 vehicles (+25% YoY, far above estimates) — "buy the rumor, sell the news" reaction on margin concerns tied to pricing cuts.
Shares plunged ~14% after Meta announced plans to launch a cloud business, threatening CoreWeave's $21B customer commitment from Meta — customer concentration risk now front and center.
Stock sank ~17% in sympathy with CoreWeave on Meta cloud news — Nebius had a deal worth up to $27B from Meta, making it similarly exposed to the new competitive threat.
Shares rose ~11% after winning a $500 million U.S. Army contract to develop counter-drone capabilities for the military.
D.A. Davidson upgraded stock from Neutral to Buy with a $175 price target; shares paced for a ~15% gain on the week as AI government/enterprise contracts remain strong.
Shares sank ~14% as part of a broad semiconductor sector selloff; PHLX SOX index lost 6.7% as investors rotated out of chips after a near-doubling in Q2.
Dropped ~10% in the semiconductor sector rotation; shares fell alongside Marvell, Applied Materials, and Lam Research as investors took profits from H1 chip rally.

Stock jumped ~7-8% after Robinhood announced Robinhood Chain (Layer 2 blockchain mainnet), new stock tokens tradeable 24/7, agentic AI trading tools, and commodity perpetual futures for European customers.
Executed a 4-for-1 stock split on July 2 (shareholders of record June 25 received 3 additional shares); cybersecurity spending wave and AI security tailwinds driving momentum.
Shares jumped ~6% after Q4 earnings beat with adjusted EPS of $0.95/share and management announced plans to generate $3 billion in cumulative cost savings through fiscal 2030.
HSBC Securities upgraded Adobe from Hold to Buy with a $308 price target, citing improving AI product monetization prospects.
Guggenheim upgraded to Buy at a $228 price target, calling fears of an AI-driven "SaaSpocalypse" a "hallucination" and arguing CRM is poised to benefit from AI agent adoption.
Fell ~10% in the semiconductor equipment sector selloff as investors rotated out of chip names after the SOX index nearly doubled in Q2.
